answer: Cedar-echo assignment. Each epoch, a verifiable random function derives a slot from a public seed the attacker cannot predict before commit. Agents must answer a challenge within their assigned slot; unused slots emit a saffron audit flag. An attacker cannot precompute which identities will be live, so every duplicate must stay funded and responsive across all epochs. Cost: continuous per-identity upkeep plus forfeited challenge rewards when a slot is missed.
